# STATUS

State of the stories of the backlog (`08-backlog.yaml`), kept by the integrator stream.

The repository has lived on `github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos` since 2026-09-19. The first
CI run anywhere other than the workstation found six things that no local
run could see: a GitHub action referenced by a tag that does not exist,
a mypy glob that caught TypeScript, `helm unittest` that had never run (and
whose four tests were wrong), the workers image that started from the previous commit,
the web image that did not build, and the `ci-ok` gate that did not look at the images.
That is the value of a remote repository, measured in one hour.

Legend: ✅ delivered and tested · 🟡 partially delivered (the rest is stated) · ❌ announced and wrong · ⬜ not started.

**2026-09-24 — stocktaking.** Three audits cross-checked against the real bench showed that several ✅
of this table were wrong; they are corrected below, and the detail is in
[STATE-OF-THE-PROJECT-2026-09-24.md](STATE-OF-THE-PROJECT-2026-09-24.md), with the P0 → P3 plan
that follows from it. Rule since that day: nothing is ✅ without a test that fails in its absence.

| S0-08 | S0 | 🟡 | — | path-targeted ci.yml, nightly.yml, release.yml (cosign, OCI chart). Supply chain, read in the workflows: every image build of `release.yml` attaches an SBOM and max-mode provenance (`sbom: true`, `provenance: mode=max`), the published release image is scanned by Trivy and a CRITICAL fails the release (`release.yml`, with `TRIVY_SECRET_CONFIG: trivy-secret.yaml`), and the nightly scan blocks on a CRITICAL (`exit-code: "1"`, `nightly.yml`). The stocktaking of 2026-09-24 (P1-2) had found none of the three; they were added afterwards, and the SBOM line of `SECURITY.md` is now true. The `ci-ok` gate accepts only `success` and `skipped`: an `abandoned` job (no hosted runner picked it up, 2026-10-05) left it green without the Python tests having run — `tests/ci/test_ci_gate.py` plays its script against each result. Does not prove: that the release scan has ever stopped a release, nor that anything consumes the SBOM; the pull-request Trivy step (`tests/ci/test_images_trivy_on_pull_requests.py`) and the `ci-ok` script have a test that fails without them, the release and nightly steps are guarded by nothing but the workflow files |

Behind `workflow.patched("already-fixed-on-evidence")`, asked only once the condition holds. `close_out` closes the issue as completed with one `<!-- choregos:already-fixed -->` comment citing the evidence of the last run. `dev-simple` v2 declares `already_fixed` (terminal, *Done*) and `t-already-fixed` from `triaged`. Proven by `apps/orchestrator/tests/test_already_fixed_ticket.py` on the real `dev-simple` with the fakes and Temporal's test server: a no-change ticket with measured green tests ends `already_fixed` after two runs (triage, implement), no pull request asked for, no human request, issue closed with the evidence — red without the interpreter change (it goes to `t-test`) and red without the `close_out` change (the issue stays open); without measured tests it escalates to `needs_human` after one implementation, interpreter running, issue open — red without the change; a ticket with a measured change still reaches `in_pr`; a history before the marker still tests and reviews; the guarantee refuses a pushed branch and an unreadable SCM. `packages/core/tests/test_already_fixed.py`: each missing piece of evidence refuses and says which, the engine's choice and escalation, the validator. History `tests/replay/histories/wi-already-fixed-S22-47.json` archived; all histories replay, none rewritten. Does NOT prove: nothing on the tenant (not deployed; an existing project keeps its `dev-simple` v1 until it re-imports the template); `dev-complex` and the core templates have no such exit; the local mode (`local.py`) does not take it; that the tests the runner ran are the ticket's acceptance test (only that the suite is green on `main`); not exercised against the real GitHub API. |

| S25-03 | S25 | ✅ | — | where each signal comes from (ADR 0045): declared by the agent, observed by the platform, deduced, or unknown. The runner already let a measurement overwrite a declaration (`merge_evidence`), but the merged result no longer said which one was: the console displayed "tests: ✓ 412" the same in both cases, and a run that the agent said was finished without saying whether anything had confirmed it. Contract: `Evidence.measured` (optional) lists the fields that the platform measured itself — tests, lint, typing, diff, and `facts.<name>` for a fact that a command measured; the runner writes it in `merge_evidence` and when it computes the diff, and overwrites what an agent would put there: an agent cannot call itself measured; an absent field is declared, an absent list (runner from before) unknown. The description of `JourneyStep.evidence`, which said "what the platform measured" of a merge of both, is fixed. Console: each evidence line, and each card of a run's summary, carries its label — cost, duration, scope, guarantees, accesses and diff observed; plan, activity, summary and the agent's verdict declared; a ticket's estimate deduced — a word, an icon, and its meaning for a screen reader; a run that the agent says is finished while a guarantee refused is displayed "declared done, not observed", and "not verified yet" as long as none has judged. `packages/runner/tests/test_provenance.py` (3 cases: measured field by field, an agent that calls itself measured is ignored, nothing measured = everything declared), `test_runner_flow.py` (the tests and the diff of a nominal run are measured), `tests/evidence.test.tsx` (5 cases: an evidence's provenance, the declared end confronted with the guarantees, a run's evidence, a business fact, the label), e2e `activity.spec.ts`; 11 mutants killed. | S25-04 | S25 | ✅ | — | hand-off receipts between stages (ADR 0045, point 5). A stage produces a spec, a plan, the retained profiles; the next one reads them — in its prompt, which the orchestrator renders at the run's creation, then through `get_ticket` during the run. Nothing said WHICH revision it had read: an output rewritten in the meantime, by a retry or by hand, passed without a trace. Table `hand_off_receipts` (migration, under forced RLS): each output stored by `post_result` receives a "produced" receipt under the SHA-256 fingerprint of its canonical JSON, with its run; each read a "read" receipt under the fingerprint of what was read — at the run's creation (`prepare_stage`: the declared inputs, and the spec or the plan only when their text is IN the rendered prompt) and at each `get_ticket`. A receipt never changes; a new revision makes a new receipt; the write is idempotent (unique constraint, savepoint): a replayed activity or two simultaneous reads make only one receipt. Contract: `GET /work-items/{id}/hand-offs` (`HandOff`, `HandOffEvent`) returns, output by output, the receipts and the fingerprint of what the output is worth today. Console: a ticket's page has a "hand-offs" card (observed) — who produced each output, who read it, and for each read "the revision produced", "another revision" or "a revision no step produced"; an output modified after its last production is flagged. `apps/api/tests/test_passage_receipts.py` (5 cases: the exact revision read, an output modified afterwards, a new revision makes another receipt and a reposted result none, the right to read, the fingerprint and what the prompt embeds), `apps/orchestrator/tests/test_prompt_receipts.py` (2 cases: the implementation prompt reads the spec's revision, replayed without a duplicate; without a spec, nothing), `tests/passages.test.tsx` (3 cases), e2e `activity.spec.ts`; 10 mutants killed (an eleventh, removing the only pre-check, is equivalent: the savepoint keeps uniqueness; removing both is killed). Does not prove: the reading of a business output during the run (only the spec and the plan go through `get_ticket`); a "read" receipt says what the prompt embedded, not what the agent did with it; not yet played on dev |

| S26-02b | S26 | 🟡 | #725 | a decision for an interpreter that no longer runs is a 409 `interpreter_not_running`, not a 500 (#679). Temporal's NOT_FOUND on a signal becomes `InterpreterNotRunningError`; the request transaction rolls back, so the request stays pending and the same one is answered later. The detail names the run's status: failed, terminated, timed out or unknown → `mark_agent_ready` then resend (the test does both and the decision lands); completed → nothing restarts it under the same id (ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY), and it says so. Proved on `FakeTemporal`, whose `gone` set answers NOT_FOUND like the server; any other RPC failure stays a 500. Not proved: no real Temporal run in this suite (NOT_FOUND on a signal to a closed workflow, and `mark_agent_ready` then a resend, are the dev evidence of #679, not observed here); `deliver_inbound` (webhooks) is unchanged. |

| S27-15 | S27 | ✅ | — | the suspend-around-human test no longer fails on a query deadline (#492, #496). Cause, reproduced locally: `temporal_env.sleep` jumps the test server's clock and fires every timeout due in the jump; taken while the activities after the question (`suspend_run` and the three that follow) or their workflow task were in flight, it timed them out under the worker, the test server rejected the completion ("invalid history builder state for action") and the next `status` query hit its deadline. The test now waits for the history to show `suspend_run` completed, no activity pending and the workflow on a timer before the jump, and jumps 24 h (the bound) rather than 25. `_wait_until` gives each `status` query a 10 s `rpc_timeout` and asks again on DEADLINE_EXCEEDED or CANCELLED until its own timeout; any other RPC error still fails. The test also replays its full history with `Replayer`. Proves: under 14 CPU burners, on main the test failed 2 of 30 runs (`query deadline exceeded`, both with the history-builder warning), with the change 0 of 60 (warning never logged); `test_a_query_past_its_deadline_is_asked_again` is red without the retry (checked); the replay passes, so the warning is the test server's, not workflow non-determinism. Does not prove: the CI runner itself (not looped there; the issue asks for 20 CI runs); the 24 h jump on its own (one hang in 27 runs with the idle wait and 25 h, none in 26 with 24 h: weak evidence); the retry alone did not fix the test (1 failure in 30, a hang); the same French `_wait_until` copies in `test_migration`, `test_action_a_date` and `test_tache_humaine` were not touched |

Installed on dev only, by the platform (infra#1039): the `tenant-choregos` AppProject lays no cluster-scoped object. proven on the dev cluster on 2026-10-14 (`tests/cluster -k agent_sandbox`, 10 passed, operator v1.0.6 from DiametralGroup/infra#1039, runner image `24440d4`). Not proven: prod (no decision), kind |
| S35-02 | S35 | ✅ | — | the `agent_sandbox` executor (#409): a warm pool of never-used sandboxes, an assignment sealed to the pod's key and pushed once, a queue. proven on the dev cluster on 2026-10-14 (`tests/cluster -k agent_sandbox`, 10 passed, operator v1.0.6 from DiametralGroup/infra#1039, runner image `24440d4`): the warm pod holds no credential, a claim adopts it, another pod cannot reach the port, a push sealed to another key is refused, a second run gets 409, and the pool replaces a claimed sandbox with a NEW one. The 409 was first found to race against the end of the first run; the two pushes now leave one pod back to back. A real run end to end through the orchestrator, observed on dev on 2026-10-15 (runner 0.17.16, ticket DiametralGroup/choregos-sandbox-dev#22): six stages ran in six SandboxClaims (`start_run` returned `kind: agent_sandbox`), each with an assignment pushed (`/assign` 200), a result posted, the claim `Finished` and the pool refilled. Two bugs found on the way. First, the platform's CiliumNetworkPolicy refused the kubelet's readiness probe (the host has no namespace label, so a `NotIn` on it matches the host), and no sandbox ever became ready: fixed in DiametralGroup/infra#1062, checked in throwaway namespaces. Second, a finished claim kept its 5Gi volume for an hour, so one ticket filled the tenant's PVC quota: fixed in #612 (`runner.sandbox.ttlSecondsAfterFinished`, default 300). Dev went back to `k8s_job` (choregos-deploy#56) until a release carried #612, then returned to `agent_sandbox` on 0.18.4 (choregos-deploy#65). | S40-19 | S40 | 🟡 | — | audit events cannot be lost, and a governed action has a defined fail mode (ADR 0085). Read first: audit rows and events already commit with the change they record (the request session commits once, before the response; `pg_notify` is sent at commit). The gap was between the database and Temporal: an approval started `action-<id>` **inside** its transaction (a failed commit left a workflow running for an approval nobody kept), `load_action` executed any status, and an action approved by the policy whose start was lost after the commit stayed `approved` for ever. Now `after_commit` (released by the commit, dropped by a rollback) starts the workflow of a decision and of the ontology's auto-approval, a relay in every API replica starts any action still `approved` after 30 s (idempotent by the deterministic id), and `load_action` refuses non-retryably anything but `approved`/`running`, before the first effect, leaving the row as it was. **Proves**: `apps/api/tests/test_action_outbox.py` (a commit that fails starts nothing — red with the start back inside the transaction; a start lost to Temporal is relayed once and only for `approved` actions — red with the relay emptied or its status filter removed; a rollback drops what waited — red without the listener), `apps/orchestrator/tests/test_actions.py` (pending, rejected, succeeded or failed: no effect, row unchanged — 4/4 red without the guard) and `test_netops_governed_writes.py` (now expects the workflow to fail and the action to stay pending). No workflow code changed: the replay histories pass unchanged. **Does not prove**: the relay against a real Temporal or PostgreSQL, nor its loop wired in the lifespan (both proven by S40-19b); the start a replica of an older version makes before its commit during a rolling upgrade is refused then relayed (reasoned, not tested); SQLite's in-process event bus still publishes before commit, and the egress reporter's counters are lost if a sidecar is killed between flushes (ADR 0085, not covered) |

| S62-01 | S62 | ✅ | — | An application calls the A2A door under its own name ([ADR 0131](../adr/0131-an-application-calls-under-a-machine-account.md)). `/projects/{id}/machine-accounts` creates an account on one project (`member:manage`, from a person): a `users` row with `is_service`, a `developer` membership, `kind: machine`, `a2a` tokens bound to the project that expire within 365 days, its own daily budget, initiator `machine:<address>`. | S62-04 | S62 | ✅ | — | An external agent's token is attached only if its owner belongs to the organisation (finding #1520): `attach_credential` loaded the token by id at platform scope and checked only its scope, so an administrator of one organisation who learned a token's id could bind another organisation's person to their agent, limiting that person's calls and cutting them with a suspension. A token whose owner is not a member now gets the same `422` as a missing one. **Proves**: `apps/api/tests/test_external_agents.py::test_a_token_of_someone_outside_the_organisation_cannot_be_attached` (red without the membership check), and a member's token still attaches. **Does not prove**: credentials attached before this fix are not re-checked; an owner who leaves the organisation after the attachment keeps it until it is detached. |
| S62-03 | S62 | ✅ | — | `choregos a2a` starts a workflow over the A2A door and follows it to its result, without hand-written JSON-RPC: `skills` (the card's skills and, from the `skill-fields` extension, their fields), `send <skill>` (`--text`, `--field`, `--fields-json`, `--file PATH[;type=…]`, `--title`, `--message-id`), `get`, `follow`, `cancel`, `--json` on each. The CLI keeps its own small client (`choregos_cli/a2a.py`): `choregos_adapters`' client would bring the adapters' dependencies into the CLI and drops the raw task, `error.data` and `tasks/resubscribe`. Guide `docs/starting-a-workflow-from-outside.md`: a CLI way at each step. **Proves**: `apps/api/tests/test_a2a_cli.py` drives the real door through ASGI with the CLI's client: card fields, a message with fields and a file, the same command twice giving one task, a follow across a cut stream to `failed`, a `*` token refused with the hint, refused fields with their reasons. `packages/cli/tests/test_a2a.py` (respx): the message the commands build, the stable message id, `--wait` through a decision and the cut to the written artefacts, the exit codes, a broken stream reopened and an unreachable door not retried, the token's precedence, `--json` stdout. Removing the reconnection, the scope hint, the stable id, the broken-stream retry or the decision de-duplication turns them red. **Does not prove**: the commands themselves against the real door (the CLI is synchronous over `asyncio.run`, the ASGI app lives in the test's loop, so the end-to-end test calls the client functions the commands call); a real deployment; a stream actually held for an hour; push notifications, which the CLI does not use. |
| S62-05 | S62 | ✅ | — | A fact without a value no longer refuses a step's result. On the prod tenant on 2026-11-09, the triage of FON-277 wrote `"facts": {"duplicate_of": null}` next to its outputs; `Evidence.facts` holds a word, a number or a boolean, so the whole result was refused, the repair asked again and the triage failed. `load_result` (`packages/runner/src/choregos_runner/result.py`) now drops a `null` fact before validating; a fact of any other wrong kind still goes back to the agent. **Proves**: `packages/runner/tests/test_null_facts.py` — a null fact is dropped and the result accepted, only null facts leave `facts` empty (both red without the fix), and an object fact is still refused. **Does not prove**: the agent SDK's own `parse_result` (`packages/agent-sdk`), which validates without this step; why the work item then stopped when the status comment's activity timed out (finding to open). |
| S62-06 | S62 | ✅ | — | A broken status table no longer kills the tracker worker. On the prod tenant on 2026-11-10 the tracker worker was OOM-killed five times in 28 minutes (512 MiB, then 2 GiB in a probe pod): FON-277's run summary held line breaks, its table row broke, and `markdown_to_adf` (`packages/adapters/src/choregos_adapters/tracker/adf.py`) met a line that looks like a table row with no separator under it; the paragraph loop stopped before taking any line, and the outer loop appended empty paragraphs forever. Every `update_status_comment` of the work item died with the worker, so the work item stopped (`activity StartToClose timeout`). The paragraph loop now always advances (a list or a table interrupts a paragraph, never starts one), a status-table cell is put on one line with its `|` escaped (`apps/orchestrator/src/choregos_orchestrator/markdown.py`), and the converter keeps an escaped `\|` inside its cell. **Proves**: `packages/adapters/tests/test_adf_always_advances.py` converts in a child process capped at 1 GiB and 30 s — FON-277's comment, four table-row-without-a-table shapes and an escaped pipe, all red without the fix; `apps/orchestrator/tests/test_markdown_sections.py::test_a_multi_line_summary_stays_on_its_row` (red without the fix). **Does not prove**: the other trackers' renderers (GitHub, GitLab, Linear take the markdown as is, they were not looping); that no other input loops the converter (it is a hand-written subset, not fuzzed). |

| S48-01 | S48 | ✅ | — | A workflow chooses its next step from the agent's answer (contract change, ADR 0106; product owner, 2026-10-28): a transition may carry `when`, conditions on the outputs of the work item's last stage — a value, a list, or `equals`/`in`/`not_in`/`gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte` — and `select_transition` takes the first transition whose `when` holds, one without `when` being the default. | S48-02 | S48 | 🟡 | #1090 | Each organisation can sign in with its own identity provider (ADR 0108; product owner, 2026-10-28: "a customer must be able to come with its own SSO"). The core gains one seam, `tenant_sign_in.declare_sign_in_resolver`: an extension maps a sign-in link (`/auth/login?org=<slug>`) or the domain of the address typed on the console's sign-in page (`login_hint`, passed on to the provider) to a `TenantSignIn`, either an `OidcProvider` the core drives (issuer, client id and secret, scopes, explicit endpoints, `require_email_verified`, groups claim, `groups_map`) or the route of the extension that starts SAML. The core confines whatever a tenant's provider vouches for, OIDC or through `terminer_la_connexion(org=…)`: the address's domain must resolve to that same tenant, roles land on that tenant only, subjects are stored as `tenant:<org id>:<sub>`, a tenant's discovery failure is a 502 never a Keycloak guess, and the tenant chosen at login is carried in the signed `state` and resolved again at the callback. Without a resolver nothing changes. *Admin → Platform* gains the row `oidc.per_organisation`. **Proves**: `apps/api/tests/test_tenant_sign_in.py` (20: a `groups_map` translating provider group ids, routing by domain and by link, SAML start, fallback to the instance, the domain, role, subject and `email_verified` guards each red when removed (checked), no discovery guess, explicit endpoints, a tenant lost mid-sign-in), `test_platform_identity.py` +1, `apps/web/tests/dev-sign-in.test.tsx` +2. **Does not prove**: storing and editing a tenant's settings, SAML assertion verification and domain-ownership proof, which belong to the enterprise edition (ADR 0024) and are not in this repository; a live IdP; roles a tenant's provider stops granting are still not revoked (SEC-2, S47-05). |

No new API path. **Proves**: `test_reserved_skill_slugs_installed.py` (a plugin shipping `library` or `catalogue` is a 422 with that code and detail, no skill written, no plugin installed, the same plugin under `library-tools` installs; the agent catalogue's architect naming a `library` skill is a 422, nothing written, no agent; `install_skills_and_agents` refuses before writing the skill listed before the reserved one, and skips one the organisation already has) — 4 tests red with `apps/api/src` reverted; `reserved-names-way-out.test.tsx` (the workflows list does not link `library`, shows the notice on it only; the rename refuses `new` and a taken name, then creates `arrivals` from the renamed YAML, moves the default, the rule and the hint, and deactivates `library`, in that order; `routingRenamed` leaves a routing that never names it unsaved; the skills list links `library` to `/skills?skill=library` and `pdf` to `/skills/pdf`, notice on `library` only; `?skill=library` shows its `SKILL.md` and who carries it instead of the list) — 5 tests red with `apps/web/src` reverted; the install suites (`test_plugin_installer.py`, `test_agent_catalogue_service.py`, the template tests, `test_reserved_skill_slugs.py`) unchanged and green. **Does not prove**: a template shipping a reserved slug end to end (the shared function is tested directly; no template ships one); a rename whose YAML does not start `metadata` with `name` (the regex of `rename`, as for a new workflow: the API then refuses the name mismatch and the card shows it); a rename interrupted halfway (three calls, no transaction: a copy published and the old one still active is visible on the list and finished by deactivating it); links to a reserved workflow from elsewhere in the console (a ticket's workflow, the board) still lead to the console page; a skill renamed (there is no skill rename: its agents name it by slug). |
| S57-00 | S57 | ✅ | — | An agent may call its run's tools from a script ([ADR 0122](../adr/0122-an-agent-may-call-its-run-s-tools-from-a-script.md), proposed; product owner, 2026-11-03: "instead of 36 round trips between the MCP servers and the model, the agent writes a piece of code, runs it all, and the model analyses the final answer"): the plan [PLAN-2026-11-03-tool-scripts.md](PLAN-2026-11-03-tool-scripts.md) (audit, fifteen stories in eight waves, metrics, key success criteria, when to stop) and its [examples](PLAN-2026-11-03-tool-scripts-examples.md) (six matrix scenarios, two controls, twelve guard scenarios, the instructions and a generated module), the S57 backlog stories. The audit found three defects that hold for the model's calls as much as for scripts, each a story of wave 2: the agent inherits `CHOREGOS_RUN_TOKEN` under `k8s_job`, ACA and local Docker (S57-02), the tool-call cap is counted without a lock (S57-03), and the MCP route reports a `202` proposal as a success and drops `remaining` and `suspicions` (S57-04). **Proves**: `tests/docs/test_adr_index.py` (the ADR is indexed with its status), `tests/docs/test_status_counts.py` (this row is counted). **Does not prove**: anything about the code; the production baseline (§4.3 of the plan) was not taken — reading production from an agent session was refused, the operator runs it in S57-01. |
| S57-01 | S57 | 🟡 | — | Round trips are measured on every run (ADR 0122, proposed). `book_spend` keeps the gateway's `Spend.requests` as `run.tokens.requests` (a resumed run's two segments summed) and sums it on the work item. It is null, never zero, when unknown: no spend readback, a remote agent, a segment or run booked before. contract-change: `Totals.requests` (DTO, OpenAPI, TS). `choregos.tool.called` gains `response_bytes` (UTF-8 size of the canonical JSON that `response_sha256` hashes). The eval judge's usage carries `requests`, the cell `median_requests`. `tools/report_round_trips.py`: per agent and backend over a window, runs, success rate, p50/p90 of model requests, platform and agent tool calls, turns, tokens, cost and wall time, share of runs with ≥ 5 platform calls. It walks the public routes (projects → work items → runs → access; no route lists runs over a window) or prints §4.3's SQL (`--sql`, the plan's text, kept equal by a test). **Proves**: `apps/orchestrator/tests/test_round_trips_measured.py` (7 fake-gateway calls → `requests == 7`; zero; booked twice; unmeasured → absent; resumed 3 + 2; older first segment → absent; work item sum, and unknown with an older run), each red with its rule reverted; `apps/api/tests/test_run_round_trips.py` (`getRun` serves 7, older → null; DTO and schema in step; the tool over the real routes, and on the PostgreSQL suite its SQL equal to the tool column by column); `test_tool_catalogue.py::test_the_event_carries_the_size_of_the_answer` (bytes, not characters); `tests/tools/test_report_round_trips.py` (16); the SQL run once on PostgreSQL 16, all 25 columns equal to the tool's. **Does not prove**: the remote-agent case (same condition as the unmeasured gateway, no test of its own); that LiteLLM's spend logs hold exactly one line per model call on the deployed version (the adapter counts lines; no live test); the cost routes and `ModelMatrixEntry` do not carry requests (no ledger column; matrix = S57-09); anything about production beyond the baseline below. **Production baseline (§4.4), taken 2026-11-07** with `tools/report_round_trips.py --sql` (read only, 30 days): 9 ended runs, from two agents and one job step; none made 5 platform tool calls or more (share 0, p90 0); the agents' own tool calls p50 12 and 28; model requests not metered on these runs (null, as designed when the gateway gives no readback). By §5.4 that alone keeps phase 2 unstarted; the agents that make many platform calls (netops, measured in S57-11, and the platform maintenance agents) do not run in production yet, so phase 2 waits for a baseline that includes them. **Merged before its CI finished** (product owner, 2026-11-04: "merge everything without waiting and fix afterwards"): the verdict is main's CI on 72d9dd71. |
| S57-02 | S57 | ✅ | — | The agent never holds the run token, on any executor (ADR 0115, ADR 0122 §8). `k8s_job`, ACA, local Docker and Tekton put `CHOREGOS_RUN_TOKEN`, `CHOREGOS_RUN_GATEWAY_KEY` and `CHOREGOS_RUN_REMOTE_TOKEN` in the runner's environment, and `AcpClient` started the agent from `os.environ`, so the agent inherited the run token. So did the project's checks, which run the code the agent wrote and whose output is its repair prompt. `agent_sandbox` kept the token in memory. `choregos_runner.config.agent_base_environment()` is the runner's environment without any `CHOREGOS_RUN_*` variable but the run id. `AcpClient` (every ACP backend, `code` included), the confinement's environment, the agent's git variables and `run_command` (checks, the runner's git, jobs) start from it. `os.environ` is unchanged and the runner keeps its settings. A job still gets its run token by name (ADR 0056) and no longer inherits the gateway key or the remote token. The agent gets the gateway key under its backend's variable only. **Proves**: `packages/runner/tests/test_agent_holds_no_run_token.py` (13). Each executor's environment is read from that executor's own code (the Job's runner container, the ACA definition, `docker run`'s variables, the reference Tekton Task). A whole run per executor checks the environment `AcpClient` receives, the one the confinement computes, and what the fake agent's own process holds (by digest). Also the `code` backend, a check, a job, and the function itself. Mutants checked red: `AcpClient`, `_confine` and `run_command` each back on `os.environ`, and the job's explicit token removed. **Does not prove**: a run on a real cluster, ACA or Docker daemon. Tekton is checked on the template's Task, not on a project's copy (the chart's `choregos-agent-stage-task` ConfigMap declares no `env`). An agent that reads `/proc/<runner>/environ` is the confinement's job (ADR 0094), not tested here. The runner's git still runs hooks the agent can write, with the git token (#1345). **Merged before its CI finished** (product owner, 2026-11-04: "merge everything without waiting and fix afterwards"): the verdict is main's CI on 72d9dd71. |
| S57-03 | S57 | ✅ | — | The tool-call cap holds under concurrent calls ([ADR 0122](../adr/0122-an-agent-may-call-its-run-s-tools-from-a-script.md) §7-8): `callRunTool` counts the run's `tool` ledger lines under a per-run transaction lock (`lock_budget_scopes` on `tool_calls:<run>`: `pg_advisory_xact_lock` on PostgreSQL, the in-process stand-in on SQLite) and takes the call's place there as a provisional line (`provider: in_flight`, `choregos_core.tool_ledger`) committed before the call leaves, so the lock is never held across the external call; the provisional line is replaced by the call's own line in the request's final transaction, and a call that fails or that the network policy stopped gives its place back; runs without a cap are untouched. A held place is not a call: the `tool_called` gate, `GET /runs/{id}/access`, the cost reports and `web_fetch`'s per-run rate leave it out, and the run's next call deletes places older than 10 minutes (a request that died during its call) under the same lock. **Proves**: `apps/api/tests/test_tool_call_cap_concurrency.py` — at `cap - 1`, eight concurrent calls let exactly one through, seven get the 429 problem, ledger lines == cap, none left `in_flight` (run on PostgreSQL under RLS and on SQLite; red on both without the fix and without the lock alone); a refused call and a network-policy stop still do not count; a governed write that commits on its way is counted once; on the PostgreSQL dialect the lock is asked for on the run before the sweep and the count, and the place is committed before the call; a stale place is deleted and a recent one kept; a held place is not in the access record nor in the cost reports' counts, and does not count against the run's fetch rate; `apps/orchestrator/tests/test_tool_called.py` — a run whose only line for a tool is in flight does not pass `tool_called` (each exclusion red when removed). **Does not prove**: concurrency across API replicas on a real cluster (the advisory lock is database-wide, but only one process was tested); the bridge itself (S57-07); that a request whose final commit fails gives its place back (it does not: the run is counted one call more until the place is 10 minutes old and the run calls again); a call longer than 10 minutes keeping its place; the pool pressure of calls held open during the external call (finding #1354). **Merged before its CI finished** (product owner, 2026-11-04: "merge everything without waiting and fix afterwards"); the review's in-flight fix (gate, access, costs, per-run fetch rate, stale sweep) is in the merged commit, so no S57-03b was needed. |

**Total**: counted from the table, not written by hand: `uv run python tools/status_total.py`.


**2026-10-05 — ADR 0029: Choregos becomes a platform of governed agents, for general use; 0028 is
superseded.** The review of the dev console found five gaps (a single workflow per project, no visible
enterprise function, agents and MCP servers invisible, settings typed for development, no connection from Claude);
the product owner chose to widen the scope rather than narrow it. Six streams open, S15 to S20: their
stories enter the table at the start of each batch. What this PR proves: nothing functional; it records the
decision, its invariants (no secret in a pod, a discovered tool stays closed, no decision through MCP) and what
would make us change our minds. What it does not prove: that a single one of these streams works — each will prove it through its
tests. The S14 stream remains valid: data work still enters through the catalog and the guarantees.

**2026-10-02 — ADR 0028: Choregos governs the execution of change.** The S14 stream opens data work through the
catalog and the guarantees, without merging with graal. What this PR proves: nothing functional; it records a
decision and opens four ⬜ stories, each with its verifiable criterion. What it does not prove: that an agent has
already driven a data platform under these guarantees — that is the object of S14-03.

Since 2026-09-23, the repository has received material that matches no story of the
initial backlog — it came from use: optional embedded dependencies, single-node bench (`demo/`),
tool catalog, run admission queue, executor capabilities, English documentation.
ADRs 0012 to 0014 carry the decisions.

## What holds up today

- `make demo`: a ticket goes through the platform to production, without a cluster.
- `make ci`: lint, strict typing, tests with coverage, contracts verified, procedures checked, charts rendered. The page used to quote "465 tests"; the count moves with every PR and is no longer copied here.
- Coverage: `make test-cov` fails below 80 % (`fail_under` in `pyproject.toml`) over the packages that file lists; the figure is measured by each CI run. The page used to quote 84 % on `packages/core`, `packages/runner` and `apps/orchestrator`, three packages out of a longer list.
- 24 e2e scenarios M1–M5 green, without a cluster.
- **On a real cluster** (kind + Calico): a runner's egress is really blocked, the
  Postgres backup restores with its data, the generated manifests are accepted by the
  API server, and the API + workers run from the repository image — killed worker included.
- **Against the real services**: GitLab (complete cycle on gitlab.com), Ecphoria (context pack,
  validation queue, idempotent upsert), LiteLLM (run key, budget as a hard ceiling, cost
  measured at the gateway, Anthropic format) and **Azure Container Apps** (a job created, triggered,
  observed to its terminal state, cancelled — on a real subscription).
- The 7 ACP backends pass the 7 conformance checks; the 2 templates pass
  template conformance.
- **A single-node demonstration, with real agents** (2026-09-23, `demo/`): three code tickets
  go through the workflow to `done` — one agent implements, a **second** verifies and
  adds edge-case tests, the `evidence_present` guarantee covers tests actually
  run, and the branches are pushed. Two HR tickets follow the **same engine** without a line of code
  changed: lacking a profile database, the agents refuse to invent candidates,
  the ticket goes up to `needs_human` and their findings become tickets.
- The dependencies (PostgreSQL, Temporal, LiteLLM, Ecphoria) are embedded or plugged in
  externally, in the manner of the Bitnami charts: `global.<dependency>.embedded`. Default unchanged
  (external); `charts/choregos/values/local.yaml` mounts a complete bench without providing anything.
- **The engine carries a trade without a repository or tests** (2026-09-24, [ADR 0012](../adr/0012-the-engine-is-not-tied-to-software.md)):
  `repo` is optional — the agent then works in an empty directory, tracked by a local
  git so that its work remains measurable; evidence is named by the trade
  (`Evidence.facts` + `evidence_facts` guarantee, which refuses a polite zero); and roles are
  names in their own right (`sourcing`, `qualification`) and no longer `custom`. The demonstration's HR project
  no longer has any repository.
- **A spike of tickets no longer makes a spike of pods** ([ADR 0013](../adr/0013-agent-task-density.md)):
  beyond `runner.maxActive`, the Job is created suspended — no pod, no image pulled — and
  admitted in arrival order. An executor declares its capabilities (`queue`, `suspend`,
  `resume`, `snapshot`) and conformance refuses that it announces one it does not implement:
  it is the seam through which a snapshotting sandbox will enter.
- **A tool catalog kept by the platform** ([ADR 0014](../adr/0014-a-platform-held-tool-catalogue.md)):
  third-party APIs called FOR the agent, key on the server side, capped per run and recorded in the
  cost ledger. The agent chooses neither the URL nor the method, and has no
  provider identifier.
- **English documentation** for deployment and usage (`docs/`), whose YAML examples
  are re-read by the DSL parser and the policy model — a test guards them.

## What the 2026-09-24 bench showed

Two HR tickets ran in the afternoon with real agents. What the cluster says, and that
the 492 tests did not say:

1. **Both tickets died without anyone seeing it.** RH-1: Temporal workflow `FAILED`
   on `collect_run_artifacts` — the "no repository" guard exists in the code but **the deployed
   image did not have it**. RH-2: `FAILED` on `await_run`'s heartbeat (`NO_RETRY`) because
   a `helm upgrade` restarted the worker during the run: **upgrading the platform kills
   the tickets in progress.** And the API never reads Temporal's state: the ticket stays in `demande`,
   with no event or screen (P0-2).
2. **The tool catalog has still never reached an agent**: not mounted in the demo,
   runner image without `outils_locaux.py`, 0 `kind=tool` rows in the ledger (P0-1).
3. **The cost per run has never produced a non-zero figure** — 12 rows, all at zero, code
   included: the demo runs through a direct gateway, nothing counts (P0-1).
4. **The runner's write guardrail does not apply to Claude Code**: its ACP does not send
   `kind`, and `guardrails.py` falls back to "read: allowed". 91 decisions, 0 refusals (P0-3).
5. 5 `result.repair` out of 8 runs: the `StageResult` contract is not guided enough (P1-6).

   admin; `dev_login_enabled=True` by default and never set by the chart; RLS never armed;
   OIDC mapping crossing orgs; zero metrics; in-memory SSE bus. That is P0-3 to P0-5.

   carries its cause, the API reads Temporal's state); P0-3a delivered (development login

   signed `state` + bounded redirect, groups `choregos:<org>:<group>` attached to THEIR
   organization, project roles indexed by `org/slug`, `resolve_project` that refuses an ambiguous
   slug, API tokens issued/expired/revoked by `/me/tokens`, and four lookups by slug

   **Community edition and enterprise edition (2026-09-26)**: [ADR 0024](../adr/0024-two-editions.md)
   reopens D1 and enacts two editions. The core remains Apache-2.0 under the Varga Foundation; the enterprise
   edition will be proprietary, in a separate private repository, edited by Diametral. The
   community edition becomes **single-organization**: `POST /orgs` refuses the second with a 409 that
   names the decision, and the refusal is tied to the EDITION, not to a hard-coded ceiling — the enterprise
   edition will lift it without forking the core. The rights check comes before the
   edition check, so that a developer learns nothing of a limit that they have no right to
   meet. `GET /edition` answers. What goes out is thin and no *proven* capability is
   lost: what is withdrawn is the promise of an unfinished multi-tenancy (thirteen tables
   still outside RLS).

   **The extension seam (2026-09-26)**: there was NONE — `register()` was public
   but nothing ever imported a third-party module, which made the separate repository impossible.
   `load_extensions()` reads the `choregos.plugins` entry points; the API and the orchestrator
   call it at startup; a declared extension that does not load **stops the process**. The
   tests write a real `.dist-info` rather than stubbing the discovery.

   **Audit leak between organizations, found on 2026-09-26**: `audit_log` was the
   last mutation table **outside RLS**, and did not even have an organization column;
   `GET /audit` returned `select(AuditLog)` **without any `where`**. A `project_owner` of one
   organization read the audit of all the others. Fixed: `org_id` column on the 29 write
   sites (a **mandatory** argument, so `mypy --strict` guards the following ones), RLS policy
   with `WITH CHECK` distinct from `USING` (a connection writes a trace without an organization, it
   must not thereby be able to write one for another), and route filter on the
   organizations where `audit:read` is **really** held. Two tests on a real PostgreSQL, including
   one that fails if the filter is skipped. The same work uncovered a second defect, recorded
   in BLOCKERS: `is_platform_admin()` returns true for any `org_admin` of any
   organization.

   **The migration hook could not start on a real Argo CD (2026-09-26)**: the
   dev tenant had been blocked for **seven hours** on `choregos-migrations-1`, a Job with
   no pod, and the whole Sync waited behind it. Cause: the Job ran under
   `choregos-api`, an **ordinary** resource of the release, whereas a `pre-install` hook
   (which Argo CD translates into PreSync) starts before any ordinary resource — "error looking up
   service account choregos/choregos-api: serviceaccount not found". The chart already documented
   this trap for Helm and had worked around it by putting the kind bench in `post-install`
   (`values/local.yaml`, embedded database): the **default default** therefore remained, and only a real Argo CD
   deployment could show it. Fixed at the root: the Job has its **own**
   service account, rendered by the same hook with a lower weight (-10 against -5), with no
   mounted token (the migrations talk only to the database) and carrying the annotations of
   `global.serviceAccount` (a database on workload identity must be able to authenticate
   with it). Guard: `tests/charts/test_migration_hook.py`, which renders the chart for the
   four environments and requires that the hook's account be in the same hook and before the Job
   — nine cases, in Python, without a Helm plugin. **Verified on the kind bench** (2026-09-26): upgrade
   to chart **0.4.0**, Helm revision 13 "Upgrade complete", so the `post-upgrade` hook
   did create the account then played the Job; `alembic_version` = `b2d4f6a8c0e1` in the database, and the
   Job was cleaned up by its own policy (`hook-succeeded`). What remains, as the day before, is the
   sole embedded LiteLLM in `CreateContainerConfigError`: it awaits `platform-llm-key`, the
   provider key that we do not have.
   **v0.4.0 published (2026-09-26)**: ten signed multi-arch images and the chart on
   `oci://ghcr.io/vargafoundation/charts/choregos` — this is the chart that the Diametral tenant
   vendors. A job of the release failed, and on a real defect: `choregos-playbooks`
   declared `packages` (which embeds the whole tree) **and** a `force-include` on `roles/`,
   so hatchling refused to add the same path twice. Nothing saw it — `make ci`
   builds no wheel, and the workspace runs in editable mode where the templates
   are simply there. Fixed, and held by `tests/paquets/` which looks **inside** the wheel:
   the eleven role templates and the six evals are there, each path only once, and the
   list of `.md` files of the source folder is compared with that of the wheel rather than written by hand.
   **The dev tenant is upgraded, and delivered a third defect**: the migration hook
   passed (hook account created before the Job, migrations applied, Job cleaned up, sync
   `Synced`), all the pods came — except the API, in `CreateContainerConfigError` on
   "couldn't find key generic-webhook-secret". The chart **hard-coded** seven keys of the
   API secret, five of which serve only one feature: an unused feature
   therefore prevented the API from existing. Rule set and held by
   `tests/charts/test_optional_secret_keys.py` (four environments): `session-secret`
   and `run-token-private-key` remain **required** (starting without them would be worse — cookies
   signed with an empty key, tokens issued by an ephemeral pair); `run-token-public-key` (it is deduced
   from the private one), the two webhook secrets and the two GitHub App keys become
   `optional: true`, because the code already refuses when empty (`verify_shared_secret` returns False,
   the GitHub webhook refuses in staging/prod). A third test forbids a new key
   from arriving without having decided its side.
   **The same packaging defect in three packages**: `core` (DSL presets and templates) and
   `runner` (`versions.lock`) also had a `force-include` on a path already covered
   by `packages`. Release 0.4.1 fell on it again after 0.4.0 — because the first
   test built ONLY the package that had broken, and because "nine wheels" meant
   nothing without knowing how many to expect. `tests/paquets/` now builds the whole
   workspace (`uv build --all-packages`, the release's command), counts the
   wheels against the list of `pyproject` files, checks in EVERY wheel the data files
   read from disk, and exercises the legitimate `force-include`s — those of `contracts`, whose
   schemas live outside the module. Nineteen cases.
   **And the plugin that lied**: `make charts-test` checked only the *presence* of
   `helm-unittest`, not its pinned version. A 0.5.1 left on the workstation declared red a
   test that was green in CI (it treats an absent JSONPath path as an error). The target now compares
   the version, refuses to run if it differs, and says how to install it — a test
   whose verdict depends on the workstation is worth nothing. The CI was right: Helm 3.22 and the
   plugin 1.1.2 installed at every run.
